issues.feedback: The spec says operators can tail logs during execution, but proposed implementation writes files only after `wait_with_output()` completes, so there is no live stream. Also, logging paths only at `debug!` may hide them in normal runs. Either change acceptance criteria to post-run capture only, or implement streaming + pre-created files and log paths at an operator-visible level.

The proposed path requires `loop_slug`, but planner output determines the slug, so it is unavailable before planner execution (one of the key debug points). The spec needs an explicit fallback path strategy for planner/prompt-review contexts (or a different context shape like direct loop-dir path).

`agent-output-<role>-<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>` can collide within the same second across retries and across acceptance QA invocations that reuse role `qa`, causing overwrite/loss. Add a uniqueness component (attempt, backend name, monotonic counter, or higher-resolution timestamp).

The spec covers non-zero exits, but not timeouts/spawn failures. With current buffered execution, timeouts are likely to produce no persisted output, which conflicts with the stated debugging need for long-running/failed invocations. Specify expected behavior for timeout/spawn paths explicitly.

Constraints say timestamp should be prefix-consistent with artifacts, but filenames in the spec use timestamp as suffix (`agent-output-role-timestamp`). This is contradictory and should be resolved in the AC.

Test plan is missing required validate conformance coverage for a new feature (per project guideline), and it does not include collision/uniqueness tests, planner no-slug path tests, timeout behavior tests, or assertions that path logging occurs at invocation start.
